Standard: The air system is functionally and logically compatible with the store to ensure SCFs between the air vehicle and the store are not negatively impacted. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Identify air system to store interface requirements that have implications to the AW of the air vehicle.
(2) Review store software documentation (e.g., OFP software version description or VDD) to verify identified store unique hazards are not inadvertently realized due to functional integration.
(3) Examine store software documentation to verify that Software Trouble Report and software anomaly reports have been corrected. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct an integration analysis, including air system databus communications and electrical interfaces, to ensure proper store operation. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct software verification testing on the store OFP for each CSCI.
    (2) Lab test: Conduct compatibility testing at the air system level.
    (3) Lab test or ground test: Perform safety regression testing IAW JSSSEH and AOP-52, Regression Testing sections as required due to hardware or software changes that affect functional integration of the store.
    (4) Lab test: Conduct fault insertion stress testing to ensure continuity, timing, sequence, fault tolerance, and ICD compliance.
    (5) Ground test: Perform a functional test of the air system and the store for software compatibility and SCF IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 102 and Flight Test Procedures appendix. Evaluate the interface between air system and store to verify proper communication and electrical interfaces between air system and store. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
(4) Review all store software documentation to ensure it is updated to reflect the configuration for operational use including Software Trouble Report, FQT, VDD, software version description and software deficiency reports (e.g., problem reports, deficiency reports, software anomaly reports) and review for residual AW hazards. Test.
(7) Lab test: Evaluate FQT conducted by the original equipment manufacturer on the store for operational store OFP IAW JSSSEH, Formal Safety Qualification Testing paragraph and AOP- 52, Functional Qualification Testing and Independent Verification and Validation section to ensure SCFs and data integrity between the air system and store interface do not result in AW hazard.
(8) Flight test: Perform captive carriage flight test prior to live fire flight test to evaluate the air system software and the store OFP to verify the data integrity, communication, and interface. Verify that the store software and air system software are compatible and there are no software anomalies that affect the AW prior to store operation.
